rec.name: Sub-Collections (Category Bubble / Title Navigation Strip)
rec.status: Built — launched (v1 tested internally and documented; v1.1 requests from the PL team still open)

what.text: A configurable Shopify section that shows a horizontal strip of category shortcuts (sub-collections). Each item has a title, a link and an image, icon or custom SVG. Two styles are available: 'Show bubbles' (round or square image above a label) and 'Show titles' (outlined, uppercase text boxes with no image). Background colour, text colour, font sizes, image sizes, gaps, alignment and positioning (static, or absolute so it overlays the hero or collection image) are all editable in the theme editor. On mobile the strip scrolls horizontally. With 4 or fewer items the strip is centred. The ticket asks for up to 20 categories.

why.text: Story-style category bubbles give shoppers a fast, visual, one-tap route into the catalogue. This cuts the clicks and decisions needed to reach relevant products, and it exposes the range of categories to people who would not open the main menu. Familiar, thumb-friendly mobile patterns (Instagram-style stories) lower friction and increase category-level engagement, which feeds PDP views and add-to-cart rate.

how.text: 1) Create the section file sections/sub-collections.liquid from the provided code. 2) In the theme editor, add the 'Sub-Collections' section to the template (e.g. under the header or hero). 3) Choose a Style (bubbles or titles), an Image style (circle or square), sizes, colours, gap, alignment and positioning. 4) Add one 'Collection' block per category with a Link and a Title, plus an Image or an SVG (the SVG overrides the image). Blocks without a link are not rendered. 5) For A/B tests, hide the section with the 'Display Section' checkbox and re-enable it for the variant with CSS: .shopify-section-story-icon-slider { display:block !important; }. A comment suggested using overflow-x:auto instead of scroll to avoid a needless scrollbar. The final code already uses auto.

items: Display Section (checkbox; can be force-shown in A/B tests via CSS)
Image size desktop (40–200px, default 80) and mobile (40–200px, default 65)
Text colour (also used for the border colour in the 'titles' style)
Font size desktop and mobile (8–50px, default 14)
Gap between items desktop and mobile (0–100px, default 10)
Positioning: Static / Absolute (overlay on the hero or collection image)
Block 'Collection': Link, Title, Icon image, SVG (HTML; overrides the image)

Requested for v1.1, not in the current code: badges (text, colours, borders), vertical offset when overlaying the hero, an optional desktop headline, more layout styles (e.g. square layouts, NaturesWay style), and highlighting the active category on collection pages with colour options

dependencies.text: No metafields or apps. The code assumes theme-specific elements: a #main wrapper, the CSS variables --menu-height and --border, and the ed-section class. Positioning and styling may need adapting per theme. Category images must be uploaded for each block. The current code has no explicit max_blocks, and Shopify's default block limit applies. The 20-category requirement is from the ticket, not from the schema. Tested in the Sectionify demo theme.

items: Bounce / exit rate on the page where the strip appears
Add-to-cart rate and conversion rate for sessions that click the strip
Mobile scroll depth within the strip (interaction rate)

images.caption: Final UI: round category bubbles with labels. The first two carry a green highlight ring, the third and fourth are plain, and the last item fades out at the edge to signal horizontal scroll.
Reference design (Warehouse theme): round image bubbles with centred labels in a light background strip. This is the 'Show bubbles' style the section reproduces.
Reference design (Showcase theme): tall square image cards with overlaid titles in a scrollable carousel. This is a layout the PL team wants to cover with the square image style.
